Messages.Author: reyda
Messages.Body:
Here is something that occured during the french open two weeks ago and
still bugs me :

Situation : at a 4 player's table, my prey has a full Arika + Matthias , 11
blood on her and 5 pool left. My grandprey ( and ally at that time) plays a
Gangrel + !Gangrel political deck. My pred plays a nosfe vote deck. I play a
malky + fleur du mal political deck. Yeah, politics everywhere.

My ally has a small gangrel out, and 10 pool influenced on one vampire, 6 on
another one. He taps his Ecoterrorists and bring up Stanislava, he then
wants to use his remaining 4 transfers to bring his second vampire,
Genevieve. That's where the nosfe player yells : "you just put Stanislava
face up, that means your influence phase is over." He calls the judge, and a
long discussion ensues : the point is he flipped up and moved Stanislava
just for convenience. (this player was not familiar with tournament
rule-lawyers)
The discussion with the judge ended when he said " this is my decision, you
can't use the remaining transfers. Go on to your discard phase."
My ally and me were very upset since by doing so the judge knew the
political balance on the table would be on the nosfe and Arika's side -the
gangrel player choose to bring out titled vamps only to counter this.
So when three minutes later my prey plays a car wrongly, i call the judge,
decided to do my lawyering better (worst?) than the others.
"Excuse me, mr judge, but this person, which happen to be my prey, played a
card in a very wrong way. The only thing he said is "I play minion tap ? any
sudden ? " He *wrongly* replaced the card. Then as we all said "no sudden",
he started to move blood counters from his vampire to his pool *illegally*.
As far as i remember, when you play a card, you must announce all terms. He
played this card illegally : decency should make you let him reshuffle this
minion tap in his library and forfeit his master phase."

The judge didn't even think about it. He saw i was playing malky and had a
prey at 5 pool. He said to my prey : " reshuffle the card *you replaced* in
your library and play your minion tap as you would have done, just announce
the total amount of blood you move from Arika".

I was uber-upset.
"Hey judge ! Where's equity ? to one guy you deny all transfers during the
transfer phase, and you let another play cards in an illegal manner ?" "but
this time it's different."
"what's different ?"

After a bit of non-gentleman arguing the game continued anyway...
What do you think about this two kind of judging depending on a mystery
factor ?
I must admit i had personnal problem with that judge that may have biased
his decision. When this kind of situation occurs and it is of public
knowledge that a judge has a problem with me, can i ask for another judge ?
what other judges would have done if they were judges on this game ?

thanks for reading all the stuff =)
reyda

While I don't have all the facts, it sounds like the judge made decisions
that fit with the facts you've provided.

The judge might have sided with the EcoTerrorist controller if that player
had convinced the judge that he was still in the middle of his influence
phase (and therefore the readying of Stanislava was illegal, since it can
only be done at the end of the influence phase). In which case the readying
of Stanislava would have been undone, and the player would've continued
with his influence phase as normal, readying Stanislava and Genevieve at
the appropriate time. But, from your description, this was not the argument
made.

The "misplayed" Minion Tap was not misplayed at all - the call for suddens
was. You cannot call for Suddens before announcing the terms of the Minion
Tap. Regardless, the replacement was also "misplayed" - you cannot replace
the Minion Tap before announcing the terms, so "undoing" the replacement
seems to be the proper remedy.

--

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
"Raille" <rai...@mich.com> wrote in message news:3DDC2F4F...@mich.com...


I think your answer is in your question. If he played the card "without terms"
then he hasn't "completely declared the effect". Rewind play to that point and
have the player correctly play the Minion Tap. He'd reshuffle the card he
replaced and possibly receive some sort of warning from the judge.

Remedying the first error by deciding for that player the target and effect of
the card would be a dangerous road to start down. For example, if a player
replaces a Govern the Unaligned before declaring "Inferior" or "Superior" would
you automatically default it to one or the other?

The next batch of tournament rules will contain some additional guidance on how
to resolve issues like this.

-Robert
--

Robert Goudie
Chairman, V:EKN
rob...@vtesinla.org

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Thursday 21 November 2002 01:01 in message
<9F_C9.1817$It3.1...@newsread2.prod.itd.earthlink.net>, Robert Goudie
mumbled something about:

> The next batch of tournament rules will contain some additional guidance
> on how to resolve issues like this.

Slap the FUCK out of the player attempting to be a rules lawyer, remove one
counter from his pool, and continue on with the game. [1.3.1.6 DSR 112002]

I'm all for not giving takebacks and the idea of "card laid is a card
played", especially in tournaments, but this particular story sets my teeth
on edge. It's not even like the guy discarded and said "Done" or anything;
he simply made the transfers he needed to bring the vampire to full. He
wasn't intending to cheat; he hadn't forgotten that he had four normal
transfers and wasn't trying to go back; he just flipped up a vampire, who,
by the rules, must enter the ready region as it now had its capacity in
blood on it.

We had a saying for this in pool tournaments; we called it "trying to win
from his chair, since he can't win at the table." While the wording
doesn't have the same ring to it when applied to V:TES, I think the intent
still carries the same weight; if someone can't win against someone else's
best game, then who's the REAL weak player, eh?

-- Derek

I agree entirely with this. The action taken by the transferring
player in this example was hardly a malicious attempt to breach the
rules was it? In friendly play (which yes, I know is not the same as
tournament play) it is quite common to see people transfer blood onto
one vamp, flip it over and then put down the rest of their transfers.
It's not that they're trying to cheat - it's probably just instinctual

In L.A., we do require players to put their blood on their vampires and then
bring them into the controlled region as oppossed to bringing them up and then
doing the influence. "Calling the judge" doesn't need to happen because someone
politely explains the rule and then we proceed. No one needs to scream out an
"AHA!" and there's no big deal made. But here's why we ask people to play by
the rules in this respect...

Have you ever influenced the wrong vampire up, or accidentally contested another
vampire? These errors never happen when you first flip and then influence.
Since we don't allow players to change their minds and redo their influence if
they accidentally contest or accidentally influce the wrong vamp we'd be, in
effect, penalizing the players who play correctly.

As Halcyan says, it only takes one black sheep. And rather than have to argue
with any black sheep about why they can or cannot redo their influence phases,
we choose to require that players influence as required by the rulebook.

-Robert
rob...@vtesinla.org

Messages.Body:

> In L.A., we do require players to put their blood on their vampires and then
> bring them into the controlled region as oppossed to bringing them up and then
> doing the influence. "Calling the judge" doesn't need to happen because someone

> Have you ever influenced the wrong vampire up, or accidentally contested another
> vampire? These errors never happen when you first flip and then influence.

Flipping (exposing the vampire to the other players) would imply making the transfers
to that vampire (unless there's some other mechanism to do so).

The only thing to be gained here would be "protection" against over-influencing him.

> Since we don't allow players to change their minds and redo their influence if
> they accidentally contest or accidentally influce the wrong vamp we'd be, in
> effect, penalizing the players who play correctly.

If the player changes her mind, she has then illegally shown a card in her uncontrolled
region to the other players.

Penalize that appropriately, and the problem is likewise solved.

Flipping the vampire up to place counters on it isn't playing incorrectly any more than
placing the Blood Doll card under rather than on top of the vampire is.

> As Halcyan says, it only takes one black sheep. And rather than have to argue
> with any black sheep about why they can or cannot redo their influence phases,
> we choose to require that players influence as required by the rulebook.

Flipping up and moving counters isn't "redoing" the influence phase.
Flipping up and then down again is.

> The only thing to be gained here would be "protection" against

If there's a gain to be made by using this particular method of influencing,
players would be wise to use it. Should I now encourage players to use this new
method since it is safer? I prefer to just ask players to influence using the
method described in the rulebook. In fact, in these parts, everyone already
does it so it's much easier to deal with.

> Flipping the vampire up to place counters on it isn't playing incorrectly any
more than

Except that no advantage is gained in the case of the Blood Doll.

How is flipping it over to put counters on it any different than the player
looking at the card, putting it back facedown, moving counters to it, and then
moving the counters back off of it to flip it up into the ready region and
move the counters back onto the card?

A: It saves time. That's all.

> Should I now encourage players to use this new
> method since it is safer? I prefer to just ask players to influence using the
> method described in the rulebook. In fact, in these parts, everyone already
> does it so it's much easier to deal with.

Ask them to do so by all means if it helps the rest of your group.
But accept their actions when taken in the spirit of the rules as well.

> > Flipping the vampire up to place counters on it isn't playing incorrectly any
> more than
> > placing the Blood Doll card under rather than on top of the vampire is.
>
> Except that no advantage is gained in the case of the Blood Doll.

OK. So we agree that it is OK to follow the spirit of the rules for
convenience's sake.
